subject: general
question: Which site provides archaeological evidence of the earliest known urban civilisation in the Indian subcontinent with planned city structures?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Harappa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Harappa**, located in present-day **Punjab, Pakistan**, is one of the most significant archaeological sites of the **Indus Valley Civilization** (2600–1900 BCE).
 
• It was among the first sites to provide evidence of a highly advanced **urban civilization**, characterized by **planned city structures**, including streets aligned in grid patterns, advanced drainage systems, and fortified areas.
 
• The discovery of Harappa in the early 20th century was instrumental in identifying the vast and complex **Indus Valley Civilization**, which is considered the earliest urban civilization in the **Indian subcontinent**.
 
• Harappa provided evidence of advanced craftsmanship, including artifacts such as seals, pottery, and tools made of stone and bronze, which demonstrated a high level of **technological development**.
 
• The site also showcased evidence of a structured **economic system**, including trade networks, agriculture, and animal domestication. This indicates its role as a major urban center in the civilization.
 
• Harappa revealed the existence of a written language, known as the **Indus script**, which remains undeciphered but is considered one of the earliest forms of written communication.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Harappa.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mehrgarh:**

 
 
• **Mehrgarh**, located in present-day **Balochistan, Pakistan**, is one of the earliest sites of human settlements in South Asia, dating back to around **7000 BCE**.
 
• It provides evidence of early agricultural practices, domestication of animals, and pottery, but it is not considered part of the urban Indus Valley Civilization.
 
 
 
• **Kalibangan:**
 
 
• Located in present-day **Rajasthan, India**, Kalibangan was another significant site of the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• It showcased evidence of **fire altars**, advanced drainage systems, and agricultural practices, but Harappa was older and more prominent in terms of urban planning.
 
 
 
• **Lothal:**
 
 
• **Lothal**, situated in Gujarat, India, is an important site known for its dockyard and evidence of maritime trade.
 
• While Lothal exhibits advanced technology and urban planning, it is not as old as Harappa and does not hold the distinction of being the earliest urban center.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of the Indus Valley Civilization:**

 
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization was one of the **three earliest urban civilizations** globally, alongside Mesopotamia and Ancient Egypt.
 
• It showcased advanced knowledge in **urban planning, metallurgy**, and trade, with a structured and complex society.
 
 
 
• **Discovery of Harappa:**
 
 
• Harappa was first excavated in the **1920s** by archaeologists such as **John Marshall** and **Rai Bahadur Daya Ram Sahni**.
 
• The excavation revealed the widespread nature of the Indus Valley Civilization, which spanned regions of present-day **India, Pakistan, and Afghanistan**.
 
 
 
• **Urban Features of Harappa:**
 
 
• Harappa’s urban planning included **grid-based streets**, multi-room houses, granaries, and public baths.
 
• The city was divided into a **citadel and a lower town**, showcasing organized social structures.
